name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.

name: Unsynchronized Access to Shared Data in a Multithreaded Context
description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

name: Improper Synchronization
description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.

evidence.explanation: CatalogService.CreateCatalogItem (65-70) reads global MAX(Id), increments it locally, then inserts and saves without a transaction spanning the read/write. Concurrent WCF request instances sharing the database can select the same next ID; primary-key enforcement rejects one write rather than preventing the race. CreateAvailableStock (99-116) also separates existence check and MAX(StockId) from insertion; StockId is explicitly DatabaseGeneratedOption.None (CatalogItemsStock 22-25). WCF per-session/per-call instance isolation does not serialize database access across clients. Confirmed non-atomic identifier allocation causes competing insert failures; database corruption or bypass of constraints is not claimed. CWE-662 and CWE-820 label the same missing synchronization defect.

name: Improper Locking
description: The product does not properly acquire or release a lock on a resource, leading to unexpected resource state changes and behaviors.

name: Missing Synchronization
description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.
